Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: No confirmed digital authentication function is available for the Mozambican national ID card. The BI is a physical card with fingerprint and photograph. The e-Government Development Index ranks Mozambique 173/193 (2023), indicating very limited e-government infrastructure. The SIGAV platform exists for passport scheduling but no online digital authentication via the national ID is documented. The EDGE project aims to develop digital authentication capabilities but this is not yet deployed.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: No government portal authentication using the national ID is confirmed. The e-visa platform (evisa.gov.mz) and the SIGAV passport scheduling platform exist but authenticate users through standard online credentials, not via the national ID. Mozambique ranks 173/193 on the e-Government Development Index. The EDGE project is developing digital government services but ID-based portal authentication has not been deployed as of 2023.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: No documented mechanism exists allowing individuals to view their own data held in the national ID database online. The Electronic Transactions Law No.3/2017 grants individuals rights to access and correct their data, and the Constitution (Article 71) provides a right of access, but there is no operational portal or system enabling individuals to access their ID data digitally. The proposed draft data protection law would establish data subject rights including access, but this is not yet enacted.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: General judicial oversight exists under Mozambique's constitution and legal system. The Constitution (2004) provides for rights protection and access to courts. DLA Piper confirms courts can issue orders regarding data access. However, there are no ID-specific judicial oversight mechanisms or specialized data protection tribunals. The draft data protection law proposes administrative enforcement by ANPD rather than judicial mechanisms. Oversight is not ID-specific.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Partial integration exists. The NUIC (Unique Citizen Identification Number) is assigned at birth and links the e-CRVS system with the national ID card. Birth certificates are prerequisites for obtaining NIDs. The UNICEF evaluation notes the 'e-CRVS system can still be better integrated with the national ID system.' INAE CRVS snapshot confirms GITEV inter-ministerial working group coordinates integration. The EDGE project (World Bank) is supporting further integration through single-window issuance. Full real-time automatic integration between CRVS and NID systems does not yet exist.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Data sharing rules are partially available. The Electronic Transactions Law No.3/2017 requires prior notification to INTIC for data processing and mandates consent for data transfers. The Constitution prohibits unauthorized access to and transfer of personal data (Article 71). Banking regulations (Notice 8/GBM/2021) require clear policies protecting consumer data. However, without a comprehensive data protection law and formal DPA, the framework is incomplete and not fully articulated for ID-specific data sharing. The EDGE project is developing a national data governance framework.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: There is no standalone Digital ID-specific regulation in Mozambique. The biometric ID card is governed by Decree No.11/2008 (general identity card decree) and the NUIC by Decree 44/2010 but these are not comprehensive digital ID regulations. The country has a draft data protection bill and is developing a data governance framework under the EDGE project, but no dedicated digital ID law has been enacted as of 2023.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The Bilhete de Identidade (BI) serves as the primary legal proof of identity for Mozambican citizens before the law. Multiple sources confirm it is required for voting, banking, accessing education, employment, health services, and formal transactions. The Global Protection Cluster briefing note (2021) states that without the BI, 'several obstacles to exercise basic rights arise, such as: to move freely, to vote, to access education, employment, healthcare, bank services.' The NUIC issued at birth is the foundational legal identifier.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Legal framework exists across multiple instruments: Decree No.11/2008 regulating the biometric identity card; Decree 44/2010 establishing the Unique Citizen Identification Number (NUIC); Civil Registration Code 12/2018 (enacted December 2018) providing the framework for civil registration and electronic CRVS; Electronic Transactions Law No.3/2017; and the 2004 Constitution (Article 71). The EDGE project is also developing additional legal and regulatory frameworks.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: Mühlbauer GmbH (a Bavarian company) holds a PPP concession (awarded 2018, 7-year contract) and established a 60-person local office in Maputo. 800 government staff were trained in all aspects of maintenance and operation, indicating partial in-country capacity. The system is operated under a public-private partnership model with extensive know-how transfer to Mozambican staff, but Mühlbauer retains technical lead. The EDGE project is further building institutional capacity.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The Bilhete de Identidade (BI) captures fingerprint data as confirmed by the Wikipedia description of the card and multiple sources. The Mühlbauer system supports fingerprint AFIS. SIM card registration (Decree 12/2023) requires both fingerprints and facial recognition, but the foundational national ID card collects fingerprints only. No confirmed iris collection for the national ID.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: The Mühlbauer system (implemented 2018-2019) provides a nationwide digital system for issuing ID cards and travel documents, distributed to 12 provinces and 177 districts with central databases. The e-CRVS system since 2018 registers births/deaths electronically. The Mühlbauer contract established four interlinked digital databases (citizen data, foreigner data, travel documents, border management). The national ID system is digital end-to-end.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Mozambique has a partially deployed biometric national ID system. The Bilhete de Identidade (BI) is issued nationally by DNIC/SNIC under Decree No.11/2008 via the Mühlbauer-built system (PPP contract 2018). Civil registration uses the e-CRVS system. However, as of 2023 coverage is ~52.9% of population and the system lacks full interoperability across agencies. The World Bank EDGE project ($150M, 2021) is actively supporting expansion. Three separate agencies manage civil registration, NID, and immigration.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: Mozambique lacks a fully operational interoperability framework. The World Bank EDGE project PID (2021) explicitly states 'the absence of an operational interoperability framework leads to wasteful duplication of efforts.' Civil registration, national ID, and immigration are managed by three separate agencies with limited coordination. The Mühlbauer system has four independently operable databases that are interlinked, but government-wide interoperability remains absent. INAGE was created to manage the interoperability platform but is not yet operational.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The Bilhete de Identidade historically had a fee (90 MTs for under-18, 180 MTs for over-18 per the Global Protection Cluster briefing note). However, since November 2023, DNIC launched a nationwide free ID campaign for all new registrations, supported by the World Bank EDGE project. The World Bank feature article (July 2024) confirms 140,000 IDs were delivered free of charge. As of 2023-2024, new ID registration is free under the campaign, though renewal and replacement may still carry costs.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Mozambique is a member of SADC (Southern African Development Community). SADC citizens do not need a visa to enter Mozambique, but cross-border travel requires a passport (not the national BI card) per accommodation/border post documentation. SADC has regional frameworks for identity document recognition. There is no confirmed formal SADC digital identity interoperability mechanism, but the Mozambican BI is recognized within some regional contexts. The Mühlbauer border management system supports ICAO-compliant travel document verification.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: The Bilhete de Identidade is typically issued to individuals 18 years of age and older (the Wikipedia article and Global Protection Cluster briefing confirm costs for under-18 and over-18 categories). The application requires a birth certificate. The BI is valid 5 years for those under 40, 10 years for those 40-50, and for life after 50. While children under 18 can technically apply, the standard eligibility threshold for the national biometric ID card is 18+. The NUIC is assigned at birth for civil registration purposes.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: The Bilhete de Identidade (BI) enrollment is not mandatory under Mozambican law. Wikipedia's list of national identity card policies indicates 'N/A' for Mozambique (not compulsory). The low coverage rate (~34-52% of adults) is consistent with optional enrollment. Citizens use voter cards and other documents as alternative identification. The World Bank and government are encouraging uptake through free ID campaigns but have not mandated enrollment.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: The BI is accepted for healthcare access. CIPESA notes the NUIC is used on 'health cards' in Mozambique. The Global Protection Cluster briefing note (2021) lists healthcare among services requiring ID. The World Bank blog (2023) confirms 'lack of identification prevents access to... health services.' The EDGE/NCRP project enabled IDPs to access 'health' services through ID issuance. However, healthcare access does not appear to be strictly mandatorily gated by the national ID — ID is accepted/beneficial but not universally required.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Some non-nationals are eligible for identity documents. The Mühlbauer system issues 'resident alien cards' and biometric emergency travel documents for foreigners. INAR (Instituto Nacional de Apoio aos Refugiados) issues identification cards to refugees and asylum-seekers. The UNHCR submission notes refugees receive identification cards issued by INAR. The Mühlbauer contract scope includes issuance of documents for foreigners. Foreign nationals holding residence permits (DIRE) are eligible for relevant documentation. Not all non-nationals qualify.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: No publicly documented independent security review of Mozambique's national ID system has been found. The Mühlbauer contract included IT security standards and training. The Greater Internet Freedom report (2023) notes the biometric system 'requires specialized hardware and software to be regularly maintained, and audited' but documents no completed audits. The draft data protection law proposes data protection impact assessments. The EDGE project includes cybersecurity components but no completed ID-specific security review is publicly documented.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: The BI is accepted (not universally mandatory) for accessing social services. The World Bank notes that without ID, citizens cannot access 'schooling, professional qualifications, land, banking, employment, or business registration.' The Global Protection Cluster briefing note confirms ID is needed for 'access to humanitarian aid.' The EDGE project combined ID and civil registration with social protection access for displaced persons. However, under the NCRP emergency project, having an ID is 'not required for displaced people to get access to basic services' in emergencies.
